topics: Tree, Depth-First Search, Breadth-First Search, Union Find, Graph
readme_description: You have n binary tree nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1 where node i has two children leftChild[i] and rightChild[i], return true if and only if all the given nodes form exactly one valid binary tree. If node i has no left child then leftChild[i] will equal -1, similarly for the right child. Note that the nodes have no values and that we only use the node numbers in this problem.

list.content:
```
Input: n = 4, leftChild = [1,-1,3,-1], rightChild = [2,-1,-1,-1]
Output: true
```

```
Input: n = 4, leftChild = [1,-1,3,-1], rightChild = [2,3,-1,-1]
Output: false
```

```
Input: n = 2, leftChild = [1,0], rightChild = [-1,-1]
Output: false
```

readme_constraints:
- n == leftChild.length == rightChild.length
- 1 <= n <= 10^4
- -1 <= leftChild[i], rightChild[i] <= n - 1
helpers_run_signature: (solution_class: type, n: int, left_child: list[int], right_child: list[int])
